```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
set.seed(123)
# Set to FALSE on Windows (DADA2 multithreading is not supported there)
use_threads <- TRUE
```

## 1. Question and data

**Question:** does the gut microbiome of one mouse differ between early
post-weaning (days 0-9) and late (days 141-150)?

**Data:** the public mothur MiSeq SOP dataset (Kozich et al. 2013): 2x250 bp
paired-end reads of the 16S V4 region, 19 faecal samples plus one mock
community with a known composition. These are raw FASTQ files.

All samples come from a single mouse over time, so the samples are not
independent. Statistical tests below are descriptive, not population-level inference.

```{r libs}
library(dada2)
library(phyloseq)
library(Biostrings)
library(vegan)
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

## 2. Download raw data and reference database

```{r download}
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)

if (length(list.files("data", pattern = "_R1_001.fastq", recursive = TRUE)) == 0) {
  download.file("https://mothur.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/wiki/miseqsopdata.zip",
                "data/miseqsopdata.zip", mode = "wb")
  unzip("data/miseqsopdata.zip", exdir = "data")
}

silva <- "data/silva_nr99_v138.1_train_set.fa.gz"
if (!file.exists(silva)) {
  download.file("https://zenodo.org/records/4587955/files/silva_nr99_v138.1_train_set.fa.gz?download=1",
                silva, mode = "wb")
}

fnFs <- sort(list.files("data", pattern = "_R1_001.fastq", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files("data", pattern = "_R2_001.fastq", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))
fnFs <- fnFs[!grepl("__MACOSX", fnFs)]
fnRs <- fnRs[!grepl("__MACOSX", fnRs)]
sample.names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(fnFs), "_"), `[`, 1)
length(fnFs)
sample.names
```

## 3. Quality inspection

```{r quality}
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:4])
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:4])
```

Reverse reads degrade earlier than forward reads, so they are truncated more
aggressively below.

## 4. Filter and trim

```{r filter}
dir.create("filtered", showWarnings = FALSE)
filtFs <- file.path("filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path("filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
names(filtRs) <- sample.names

out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs,
                     truncLen = c(240, 160), maxN = 0, maxEE = c(2, 2),
                     truncQ = 2, rm.phix = TRUE, compress = TRUE,
                     multithread = use_threads)
head(out)
```

## 5. Denoise, merge, remove chimeras

```{r dada}
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, multithread = use_threads)
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread = use_threads)
plotErrors(errF, nominalQ = TRUE)

dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err = errF, multithread = use_threads)
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err = errR, multithread = use_threads)

mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs)
seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method = "consensus",
                                    multithread = use_threads)

dim(seqtab.nochim)
sum(seqtab.nochim) / sum(seqtab)   # fraction of reads kept after chimera removal
```

### Read tracking through the pipeline

```{r track}
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))
track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN),
               sapply(mergers, getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim))
colnames(track) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR",
                     "merged", "nonchim")
rownames(track) <- sample.names
track
```

## 6. Accuracy check on the mock community

```{r mock}
mock.ref.file <- list.files("data", pattern = "HMP_MOCK", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)[1]
mock.ref <- getSequences(mock.ref.file)

unqs.mock <- seqtab.nochim["Mock", ]
unqs.mock <- sort(unqs.mock[unqs.mock > 0], decreasing = TRUE)
cat("DADA2 inferred", length(unqs.mock), "sequence variants in the mock community.\n")

match.ref <- sum(sapply(names(unqs.mock), function(x) any(grepl(x, mock.ref))))
cat("Of those,", match.ref, "matched exactly to expected reference sequences.\n")
```

## 7. Taxonomy and phyloseq object

```{r taxa}
taxa <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim, silva, multithread = use_threads)

samples.out <- rownames(seqtab.nochim)
subject <- sapply(strsplit(samples.out, "D"), `[`, 1)
day <- as.integer(sapply(strsplit(samples.out, "D"), `[`, 2))
samdf <- data.frame(Subject = subject, Day = day, row.names = samples.out)
samdf$When <- ifelse(samdf$Day > 100, "Late", "Early")

ps <- phyloseq(otu_table(seqtab.nochim, taxa_are_rows = FALSE),
               sample_data(samdf), tax_table(taxa))
ps <- prune_samples(sample_names(ps) != "Mock", ps)
ps <- subset_taxa(ps, Kingdom == "Bacteria" & !is.na(Phylum))
# Remove mitochondrial and chloroplast sequences (not part of the gut community)
ps <- subset_taxa(ps, (is.na(Family) | Family != "Mitochondria") &
                      (is.na(Class) | Class != "Chloroplast"))
ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)

dna <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(taxa_names(ps))
names(dna) <- taxa_names(ps)
ps <- merge_phyloseq(ps, dna)
taxa_names(ps) <- paste0("ASV", seq(ntaxa(ps)))
ps
```

## 8. Composition

```{r composition}
ps.prop <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(x) x / sum(x))
top20 <- names(sort(taxa_sums(ps.prop), decreasing = TRUE))[1:20]
plot_bar(prune_taxa(top20, ps.prop), x = "Day", fill = "Family") +
  facet_wrap(~When, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(y = "Relative abundance", title = "Top 20 ASVs by Family")
```

## 9. Alpha diversity

```{r alpha}
alpha <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))
alpha$When <- sample_data(ps)$When

plot_richness(ps, x = "When", measures = c("Observed", "Shannon")) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = When), alpha = 0.4)

wilcox.test(Shannon ~ When, data = alpha)
wilcox.test(Observed ~ When, data = alpha)
```

## 10. Beta diversity

```{r beta}
ord <- ordinate(ps.prop, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")
plot_ordination(ps.prop, ord, color = "When") +
  geom_point(size = 3) + stat_ellipse() +
  labs(title = "PCoA, Bray-Curtis")

bray <- phyloseq::distance(ps.prop, method = "bray")
meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps.prop))
adonis2(bray ~ When, data = meta, permutations = 999)

# Check the dispersion assumption of PERMANOVA
anova(betadisper(bray, meta$When))
```

## 11. Differential abundance (DESeq2)

```{r deseq}
dds <- phyloseq_to_deseq2(ps, ~ When)
dds <- DESeq(dds, sfType = "poscounts")
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("When", "Late", "Early"), alpha = 0.01)

sigtab <- as.data.frame(res[which(res$padj < 0.01), ])
sigtab <- cbind(sigtab, as.data.frame(tax_table(ps)[rownames(sigtab), ]))
sigtab <- sigtab[order(sigtab$log2FoldChange), ]
nrow(sigtab)

ggplot(sigtab, aes(x = reorder(rownames(sigtab), log2FoldChange),
                   y = log2FoldChange, fill = Family)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "ASV", y = "log2 fold change (Late vs Early)")
```

## 12. Limitations

- One mouse sampled repeatedly: samples are autocorrelated, so p-values are
  descriptive. A real study would need multiple independent animals.
- ASVs are compared by relative change only (compositional data).
- Taxonomy is only as good as SILVA v138.1 at genus level for a ~250 bp V4 region.
